questions.q: What does a `resource` block tell Terraform to do?
options: Only read information about something that already exists, without ever changing it
Generate a report listing every resource in the subscription
Create the declared resource and manage it going forward — deleting the block and re-applying destroys the real thing
Permanently lock a resource so it can never be destroyed
questions.explain: A resource block is a standing instruction for what should exist; Terraform treats it as something it owns, including destroying it if the block is removed.

questions.q: What happens to the real cloud resource if you delete a `data` block and run terraform apply again?
options: Terraform refuses to run apply until the data block is restored
Terraform recreates the resource under a new name
Nothing — Terraform simply stops reading that resource; it never created or managed it
The real resource is destroyed, the same as deleting a resource block
questions.explain: A data source only reads information about something that already exists — Terraform never creates, changes, or destroys what a data block refers to.

options: A list of every provider available in the Terraform Registry
A JSON record of every resource Terraform manages and the last real-world values it knows for each one
The raw HCL source code of the configuration
A cached copy of the Azure Portal's UI
questions.explain: State records IDs, computed attributes, and dependency relationships for everything Terraform is managing — written every time apply runs.

questions.q: What is the supported way to inspect what's currently tracked in state, according to this lesson?
options: Running terraform destroy and reading the output
Opening terraform.tfstate in a text editor and modifying values directly
terraform state list and terraform state show <resource>, rather than hand-editing terraform.tfstate directly
There is no supported way to inspect state
questions.explain: terraform state list and terraform state show are the supported inspection commands; hand-editing the state file is explicitly discouraged.

questions.q: When terraform plan decides what to create, update, or destroy, what is it actually comparing your configuration against?
options: The .terraform.lock.hcl file
The state file — not directly against whatever is currently live in the cloud
A cached copy of last week's plan output
Nothing — plan runs purely on the configuration with no comparison at all
questions.explain: Plan and apply always diff declared configuration against state, which is why a lost or corrupted state file leaves Terraform without a memory of what it's managing.
